reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown treat the wicked's long life as only apparent, since against eternity even a long life is short, so Job and the wisdom maxims agree.

discrepancy.note: Troki answers a Christian's prosperity argument by noting many wicked men, like Nebuchadnezzar, prosper while the pious suffer affliction.

quotes.text: in this world there are many wicked men, whose lot is as prosperous as if they were truly righteous men, while we frequently see the pious labouring under severe afflictions
quotes.attr: Isaac ben Abraham Troki (d. 1594), Faith Strengthened (Chizzuk Emunah), trans. Moses Mocatta (1851), ch. V, on Job 21:7.

sides.snippet: Why do the wicked live, Become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?
sides.verseText: \"Why do the wicked live, Become old, yes, and grow mighty in power?

sides.snippet: it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow
sides.verseText: But it shall not be well with the wicked, neither shall he lengthen days like a shadow; because he doesn't fear God.
